content.title: About
content.content: The Italian sandwich on white bread (1823) is a classic sandwich made with thinly sliced ham, mozzarella cheese, tomato, fresh basil leaves, and extra‑virgin olive oil, placed between two slices of soft white bread. It combines the freshness of vegetables with the aromatic profile of Mediterranean ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is listed as number 1823 in the traditional Italian snack catalog.
A crust‑less white bread is traditionally used to highlight the softness of the filling.
The mozzarella‑basil combination originates from the classic Caprese salad.
First‑cold‑press olive oil gives the sandwich its characteristic Mediterranean aroma.
A version with added prosciutto is considered a premium variant and is often served in restaurants.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham and bread provide B1, B2, and B6 vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Mozzarella and ham supply high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olive oil is high in oleic acid, which promotes heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants from tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes contain lycopene, an antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain diseases.

items.title: Calcium from mozzarella
items.content: Mozzarella provides a good amount of calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham and cheese can be high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Mozzarella may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich is relatively calorie‑dense due to oil and cheese; portion control is advised for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Nitrite presence
items.content: Some cured hams contain nitrites, which should be limited in large amounts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the sandwich fresh, cut diagonally into halves. Optionally sprinkle with freshly ground black pepper or a drizzle of balsamic vinegar. It pairs well with a light salad or sparkling mineral water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich refrigerated at 0‑4 °C and consume within 24 hours. If ingredients are stored separately, keep bread in a dry place and ham and cheese in airtight containers.
